title: Round 3: Design a scalable order-processing system
description: Design an order-processing system that can handle thousands of orders per minute while keeping inventory consistent and payments reliable.

data.text: The interviewer asks you to design a system that accepts orders from a storefront, checks inventory, processes payment, and arranges fulfillment. The twist is scale: the system must handle Black Friday traffic without double-selling items or losing orders.

items: Customers can browse products and place orders with multiple line items
Inventory must not go negative: two customers cannot buy the last item simultaneously
Payment must succeed or fail atomically with the order state
The system must remain available even if one downstream service is slow
Order history must be queryable by customers and operations staff

data.text: Before you draw boxes, write down the requirements you would clarify. Will orders be international? Do you need returns? What is the acceptable delay between payment capture and fulfillment? These questions show that you think about edge cases.

data.title: Simplified order flow
data.content: A typical happy-path flow spans several services:
data.code:
1. Frontend sends order to Order Service
2. Order Service reserves inventory in Inventory Service
3. Order Service charges payment in Payment Service
4. Order Service publishes OrderConfirmed event
5. Fulfillment Service consumes event and schedules shipping
6. Notification Service sends confirmation email

cards.title: Synchronous orchestration
cards.description: The Order Service calls inventory, payment, and fulfillment in sequence inside a single database transaction.

cards.title: Event-driven choreography
cards.description: Each service listens for events and acts independently. Inventory emits Reserved, Payment emits Charged.

data.title: Embrace eventual consistency
data.text: In a high-scale order system, it is usually better to accept eventual consistency than to block the customer while every service confirms in sequence. Explain how you would communicate the delay to the user and how you would compensate if payment fails after inventory was reserved.

data.title: Summary
points: Choose orchestration for simplicity, choreography for scale
Address inventory consistency with reservations or sagas
Plan for failure at every step
data.takeaway: A scalable order system is less about any single technology and more about choosing the right coordination pattern for your team size and traffic profile.
